subject: Make Polluters Pay Bill Endorsement
overview: The committee discussed local sustainability initiatives, voted to endorse state legislation establishing a climate change superfund targeting fossil fuel companies, and reviewed annual priorities alongside an educational presentation on environmental neurotoxins.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The committee approved the minutes from the previous meeting.

items.title: Administrative Updates and City Initiatives
items.summary: Brenda Pike reported on the upcoming May 6 meeting with Senator Mike Barrett, progress on the Electrify Medford contract, electricity aggregation bids, expanding curbside composting, and the city's pursuit of state Climate Leader certification.

items.title: Resolution on Climate Change Superfund Bill
items.summary: The committee passed a motion endorsing state legislation (H.872/S.481) to establish a climate change superfund and polluter responsibility program.

items.title: Discussion of Committee Priorities
items.summary: Members discussed outreach strategies, including launching an Instagram channel and collaborating with schools to plant urban meadows and pollinator gardens.

items.title: Presentation on Environmental Chemicals and Neurodevelopment
items.summary: Paul presented scientific research regarding the toxic effects of quaternary ammonium disinfectants and organophosphate flame retardants on brain oligodendrocytes.

items.title: Tree Ordinance and Shade Tree Distribution Update
items.summary: Brenda Pike reported that tree ordinance drafts are expected within a month and noted that 54 free shade trees were recently distributed to Medford residents.
